title: Taxi dance band lineup, hours and pay
summary: Three altos, rhythm section, nightly schedule, union hours and $60 a week.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: That's the time when, uh, Albert Walters took sick, he was on that job. He took sick, and he got John Penny. And one time we had sports, Sun Johnson, and, and, uh, John Handley. Three alto saxophone, working at Taxi Dance. Taxi Dance is a hard thing.
Yeah, well I can't imagine them having three men. Three alto saxophone.

Three alto saxophone. Mm. Got a drummer by the name of Papa, I know you heard of him. Yeah. His last name was, his name was Eddie Smith. I don't remember that. With Octavia Crosby on the piano. When I first went to the front, they had Walter Decoe. He's the one that killed that man. Mm-hmm. Then we had a Shoemaker. He was a wonderful piano player, but I just can't call his, his name now. Mm-hmm. Was playing the piano.
Well how did those three saxophones work? Did they all play one?

They sound good, they harmonize together good. Mm-hmm. And we, on the end, we had tenor, Clown's Hall. Mm-hmm. Clown's Hall working the day at Illinois Central Railroad and work every night with us down there. That was the whole, that went through all the whole week that you all? Every night. You didn't have a night off? Mm-hmm. I had Monday night off. Yeah. Somebody paid the place? Everybody, yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Uh, Buddy Charles used to be in there sometime, used to get, get Flusia, Sidney Flusia to come back. Old man Johnnie Censie or somebody like that, you know, to come and make that night. But nobody wanted me, because it was so hard.
Oh yeah. He didn't pay that much?
I would give him $60 a week. I was looking for my income tax people back there to find, but I couldn't find them for y'all.

$60 a week was good money then. Yeah. Oh yeah. In the forties. What did you have a long lunch hour on a job like that? Yeah, an hour. I'd give him an hour. Well who would play guitar when you were out?

They didn't use the guitar. Oh I see. Octave played the piano. I see. And when, when Octave go, I just play the guitar until he come back, you see. Unless somebody was a piano player like Drew Robson or someone would stop in, you know.
How long was the job? How many hours?

When I first started at that job, it was from 8 o'clock to 5. What? And then the union came in and. That's 9 hours. Yeah. But. The union come in and, the union come in and, and, and, and, and, and, and started making them heavy from 9 to 2. That's why I asked him about lunch hour. One hour.
Well, yeah. But what did the drummer do? You had to have drums, huh? For lunch hour. Play without drums.
Play without drums. Play without drums. Yeah, they have just, it's an hour in lunch hour. 9 to 2.
Unless, uh. I wasn't too bad.

Unless sports go back there on the drums, you know, somebody could play a little. William Young, he'd go back there, you know, he's a leader, you know. Yeah. Keep a little time until he come back. Yeah, Handy could play drums. John Handy could play drums. Well, he never detested, so, and, Handy kept the bottle in his hand all the time. Yeah.
